items.headline: Jankowski scored a power-play goal in Saturday's 3-2 win over the Jets.
items.text: The 32-year-old center continued his remarkable run, getting Carolina on the board midway through the second period with a quick shot through traffic past Clay Stevenson. Jankowski has found the back of the net in six straight games -- not bad for a bottom-six player who scored a grand total of 11 goals over 68 regular-season games in 2025-26. Saturday's tally was also Jankowski's first power-play goal since 2017-18 with the Flames, and just the third of his career. He is getting extra shifts and opportunities with Jordan Staal (calf) on the shelf, but shooting at a 40.0 percent rate simply isn't sustainable.

items.headline: Jankowski score a goal on two shots in Tuesday's 4-2 win over the Capitals.
items.text: Jankowski extended his scoring streak to five games (five goals, one assist). And with news of Jordan Staal's (calf) multi-month absense, the pivot is going to see continued opportunity and ice time. Jankowski's face-off effectiveness is less than ideal (44.4 percent), but he could provide depth offense in deep formats.

items.text: Facing the franchise he made his NHL debut with back in 2015-16, Mantha helped set up an Evan Rodrigues tally early in the first period to open the scoring, then notched his own midway through the second frame. The 32-year-old winger is coming off a career-best 33 goals and 64 points in 81 regular-season contests for Pittsburgh in 2025-26, but his middle-six role in New Jersey and lack of consistent power-play time will make it very difficult to repeat those numbers.

items.headline: Maccelli scored a goal, registered an assist, posted a plus-2 rating and launched six shots on net in Tuesday's 3-2 win over the Canucks.
items.text: Maccelli played a large part in Tuesday's win, as he tallied the Islanders' second goal of the opening period before helping them reclaim the lead early in the third with the primary helper on Kyle Palmieri's go-ahead score. With Tuesday's performance in the books, the 25-year-old Maccelli has a goal, five points, a plus-2 rating and 12 shots on net across six outings. He's been grinding on the team's fourth line to keep his role as a depth winger over Kyle MacLean. Maccelli's current four-game point streak is one of the best of his six-year NHL career, and it's helping him trend towards fantasy relevance as a streaming option in deep leagues.

items.headline: Tavares sustained an undisclosed injury in the third period of Thursday's game versus the Sabres, and head coach Jim Hiller had no update on the center's status following the contest, David Alter of The Hockey News reports.
items.text: Tavares collided with a Sabre and came away worse for wear, leaving the game immediately. The Maple Leafs should know more in the coming days regarding the 36-year-old's status. Toronto hosts the Islanders on Saturday. Tavares had two assists prior to his exit, giving him seven points through seven contests this season.

items.headline: Tavares scored a goal and added an assist, both on the power play, in Tuesday's 5-4 loss to the Mammoth.
items.text: Tavares was out of the lineup Saturday for the birth of his fourth child. He rejoined the Maple Leafs for the last game of their road trip and delivered a strong performance with his first multi-point effort of the season. The 36-year-old center is up to two goals, three assists, 17 shots on net and a minus-5 rating over six appearances. Tavares will continue to see steady time on the second line and first power-play unit.

items.headline: Tavares (personal) participated in Monday's practice, per David Alter of The Hockey News.
items.text: After missing Saturday's 6-3 win over Colorado for personal reasons, Tavares should return to the lineup against Utah on Tuesday. He has registered one goal, two assists, 14 shots on net, four blocked shots and three hits in five appearances this season.

injuries.longComment: Less than 24 hours after Merzlikins was traded to the Maple Leafs, a timetable for his return to action has been provided. The 32-year-old backstop had an up and down season in 2025-26, where he posted a 14-11-3 record, a 3.39 GAA and an .883 save percentage across 30 regular-season outings. He won't be rushed into action, as the Leafs new goaltender tandem of Sergei Bobrovsky and Anthony Stolarz are still expected to handle the majority of reps between the pipes this upcoming season. However, when Merzlikins is ready to return, he's the clear No. 3 option in Toronto's organization and could still see some playing time at the NHL level if he isn't sent down to AHL Toronto.
injuries.shortComment: Merzlikins is expected to miss 4-6 months to begin the 2026-27 regular season while recovering from a shoulder injury, per Luke Fox of Sportsnet.

items.text: Roy has been sidelined since early October due to his upper-body injury, but he appears to be close to returning to game action. Even if he doesn't get the green light to suit up against New Jersey, it seems possible that he'll be cleared to return at some point next week. Across his first two regular-season appearances, he was held scoreless with five hits and five blocked shots while averaging 18:26 of ice time.

items.headline: Head coach Spencer Carbery said Friday that Sourdif (illness) is considered day-to-day, Sammi Silber of The Hockey News reports.
items.text: Sourdif didn't practice Friday due to his illness, and it's unclear whether the issue will impact his availability against New Jersey on Saturday. Pierre-Luc Dubois (illness) has already been ruled out for Saturday's matchup, so Ethen Frank will likely see playing time for the Capitals if Sourdif is sidelined. Regardless of Sourdif's status for Saturday's matchup, it's at least encouraging that the 24-year-old doesn't appear to be facing a long-term absence.

items.headline: Sourdif didn't participate in Friday's practice session due to an illness, Tom Gulitti of NHL.com reports.
items.text: Sourdif hasn't yet missed a game to begin the regular season, recording a goal, 13 hits, eight PIM and two blocked shots while averaging 13:24 of ice time. It's not yet clear whether he'll be available for Saturday's game against the Devils, but Ethen Frank will be a candidate to enter the lineup if Sourdif is sidelined, especially if Pierre-Luc Dubois (illness), who also missed Friday's practice session, remains out.
